rules.title: Production telemetry is read from the instrumentation that already exists, and adds no probe site to the measured path
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no APM extension in the request path and no userland StatsD or OpenTelemetry client to reconcile with it; the runtime's own probes are the only instrumentation

rules.title: A trace id exists for every request whatever the sampling decision, and it is the only request identifier
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no `X-Request-ID` read or minted; the W3C trace id is the request identifier a log line, an error rendering and a proxy all share

rules.title: A log record inside an active trace carries `trace_id` and `span_id`, and outside one omits both rather than writing them empty
rules.divergesFromPhp: `error_log` writes no correlation id; every JSON-Lines record written inside a traced request can be joined to its trace from the line alone

rules.title: `Core\Metrics` is three verbs for three kinds, always present, and accumulates whether or not an exporter is built
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no client library to install and no `record(name, value, kind)`; a counter, a histogram and a gauge are three members, and a name is validated at a literal call site

rules.title: Ten series exist the moment an exporter is configured, with no application code written
rules.divergesFromPhp: request rate, latency, query time, GC pause and spawn overhead are on the scrape endpoint before the application emits anything, where PHP needs an APM agent or a hand-written StatsD client for the first three and cannot reach the last two at all

rules.title: A metric name is fixed to one kind and one label set on first use, and a second kind throws naming both sites
rules.divergesFromPhp: recording one name as a counter here and a gauge there is a throw at the second call, not a series the backend quietly reports twice

rules.title: The `route` label carries the route's declared name, never the request path, and a route without one has no label
rules.divergesFromPhp: a series is keyed by the route's compiled name rather than by the request path a StatsD client would key on, so `/users/1`, `/users/2` is one series and not one per user

rules.title: A metrics registry is per core, merged at scrape, and no program reads a metric
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no APCu-style shared counter store; every core keeps its own approximate aggregate and the merge is arithmetic at scrape time

rules.title: Past `max_series` a new series is refused and an existing one is never evicted
rules.divergesFromPhp: past the cap the newest label set is dropped with a warning, not the oldest evicted; a counter never appears to reset

rules.title: `[metrics]` and `[trace]` are `System` blocks, and a value neither exporter accepts is refused at boot
rules.divergesFromPhp: a request cannot switch tracing on for itself the way `xdebug_start_trace()` or an `ini_set` can; where telemetry ships is the deployment's decision

rules.title: Exactly four things become a span, and a `call` event never does
rules.divergesFromPhp: a distributed trace is not Xdebug's per-call function trace; a span is a request, a query, an outbound call or a spawn, and nothing finer

rules.title: A `call` event never becomes a span; the root, a `query`, an outbound HTTP call and a `spawn` do, and `gc` becomes a metric
rules.divergesFromPhp: an OpenTelemetry SDK installed as a library lets a program open a span around any function; here the set of things that become a span is closed and a function call is not in it

rules.title: A trace event carries one of five kinds — `call`, `gc`, `spawn`, `query`, `http` — and a `call` keeps its probe shape
rules.divergesFromPhp: Xdebug's trace is a log of function calls; here a collector pause, an isolate spawn and a database statement are events of their own on the same stream, tagged so a viewer can tell them apart

rules.title: A statement is a `query` trace event that carries its duration, driver, connection, truncated SQL and row counts, and never a bound parameter
rules.divergesFromPhp: there are no mysqlnd statistics and no general query log; a statement is a trace event, filed in the driver and off the hot path, and it never carries a bound value

rules.title: A `[db.<name>] slow_query` threshold writes a statement's span facts to `Core\Log`, and is off until a block writes one
rules.divergesFromPhp: the slow-query log is a per-connection threshold in `nvs.toml` written by the application's operator, not the server's `slow_query_log`, and it reports the same facts the trace does

rules.title: A collector pause is a `gc` event recorded from the collector's run routine, never from the safepoint poll
An isolate spawn and its join are one `spawn` event naming which of the three forms it was, with an overhead split, and a child's own stream never crosses live
An inbound `traceparent` is continued, and one the process cannot read starts a new trace rather than failing the request
`Core\Http\Client` sends `traceparent` while `[trace] propagate` is on, and the id it sends is the request's own
rules.divergesFromPhp: a trace crosses a service boundary with no header code in the application, where a PHP client has to be wrapped to carry one

rules.title: Sampling is decided once at the root by `[trace] sample`, and an inbound trace that is already sampled is always continued
The exporter is a feature-gated Native subsystem, and `Core\Metrics` is Tier 0 in every build
The OTLP and Prometheus paths are dependencies; the event-to-span wiring and the per-core registry are ours
The four event kinds export as one speedscope evented timeline, beside Callgrind, Clover/lcov and NDJSON
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no Xdebug cachegrind file to open in a bespoke viewer; the timeline is speedscope's open evented format, the same file the sampling profiler writes

rules.title: A request reads its own memory as `memoryHeld`, `memoryPeak` and `memoryLimit` on `Core\Budget`, and the process's resident bytes are `Core\Os`'s
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no `$real_usage` boolean and no second accounting behind it: `memory_get_usage`'s two numbers were one member with a flag, where the request's held bytes and the process's resident set are two members on the two classes that own them

rules.title: The runtime records a request's memory high-water mark in every build, and a nested isolate restores the enclosing mark rather than clobbering it
rules.divergesFromPhp: `memory_get_peak_usage` reads a mark PHP keeps because its allocator holds its chunks; here the mark is kept deliberately, because deterministic release means the current figure falls back to the baseline and hides the spike

rules.title: A `[limits] memory_high_water` fraction writes one `Warn` when a request's memory peak crosses that share of its ceiling, and is off until a block writes one
rules.divergesFromPhp: PHP has no warning short of the fatal: a request that touched 96% of `memory_limit` and returned successfully is indistinguishable from one that never passed 30%

rules.title: `Core\Script::onExit` registers a request-local hook that runs FIFO as the last user code, and each hook receives one readonly `ExitReport`
rules.divergesFromPhp: `register_shutdown_function` is gone; the hook takes a typed `Script\ExitReport` with the reason, the status and the live `Throwable`, where PHP reads `error_get_last()`

rules.title: The exit queue drains once — at a normal end, at `exit` and at an uncaught throw — and the report says which ending it was
Exit hooks run after every `finally` and after the failure hooks, and before native teardown, with the heap alive and output where it was
A `FATAL` and a cancellation run no exit hook — `Core\Fatal::onLimit` is the one observer of a limit breach
rules.divergesFromPhp: PHP's shutdown functions fire on most fatals; here a resource-limit `FATAL` reaches only `Core\Fatal::onLimit`, and a migrator moves that one use there

rules.title: A hook observes the ending and never steers it: the report is fixed first, a throw is logged and abandoned, `exit` inside a hook throws, and the drain continues
rules.divergesFromPhp: a shutdown function in PHP can call `exit` to change the status or silently swallow the pending error; here neither is possible
